item.title: Pope Leo at 300 Days: ‘Vatican II, Part Two’ - CathNews
item.description: More than 300 days into his papacy, Pope Leo XIV is being described by a longtime Catholic social justice scholar as a man who understands that faith must be lived in the world, not sealed off from it. Source: Common Home TV.

item.title: Mater Hospital opens $42 million palliative care centre - CathNews
item.description: A $42 million state-of-the-art palliative care facility and day surgery centre has been opened at St Vincent’s Mater Hospital in Wollstonecraft. Source: The Catholic Weekly.

item.title: Forums discuss Victoria’s needs ahead of state election - CathNews
item.description: Ahead of the Victorian state election in November, Catholic Social Services Victoria invited leaders from across its membership, alongside colleagues from Catholic education and health, to discuss core areas of need in the state.

item.title: Gambling companies using female celebrities, influencers to target women - CathNews
item.description: Reform advocates, medical professionals and crossbenchers are teaming up to push for action on gambling as a landmark report on its harms gathers dust 1000 days on. Source: Canberra Times.

item.title: ‘Mass for You at Home’ comes to the Pilbara - CathNews
item.description: Easter is a time of joy, hope and celebration – and for the people of the Pilbara, it’s a special moment in television history. Source: ACBC Media Blog.

item.title: Water contaminated, food access interrupted in far-north communities - CathNews
item.description: Church communities across the far north of the country are boiling water to drink after access to essential goods was affected by ex-Tropical Cyclone Narelle. Source: The Catholic Leader.

item.title: CathNews takes Easter break - CathNews
item.description: CathNews is taking an Easter break and will not be published on Good Friday or Easter Monday.

item.title: Bangladeshi Christians demand Easter Sunday holiday - CathNews
item.description: Christians in Bangladesh formed a human chain and rally in the capital this week demanding that the government declare Easter Sunday a public holiday. Source: EWTN News.

item.title: Childhood favourites come to life in magical adventure - CathNews
item.description: Three Enid Blyton novels are covered in 'The Magic Faraway Tree' and they take place in an enchanted forest where a huge magical tree grows, which titles the film. Source: Australian Catholics.

item.title: Catholics urged to support Collection for the Holy Land - CathNews
item.description: Support for the annual Good Friday Collection for the Holy Land remains vital, especially amid the ongoing conflict in the region, said Cardinal Claudio Gugerotti, Prefect of the Dicastery for the Eastern Churches, in a recent letter to the entire Catholic Church. Source: Melbourne Catholic.

item.title: Vinnies launches plan to combat homelessness in Victoria - CathNews
item.description: The St Vincent de Paul Society Victoria yesterday launched a call to action ahead of the state election, calling on all parties to commit to a long-term housing strategy focused on prevention, housing supply and community support.

item.title: Pope Leo to wash feet of newly ordained priests - CathNews
item.description: Today, on Holy Thursday, Pope Leo XIV is set to wash the feet of 12 priests during the Mass of the Lord’s Supper in the Basilica of Saint John Lateran. Source: Vatican News.

item.title: Enjoy Easter and prepare for tough times ahead: PM - CathNews
item.description: Anthony Albanese has urged Australians to go about the Easter weekend as normal, but warned about grim times ahead and tougher measures to conserve fuel in a rare address to the nation. Source: SMH.

item.title: Sydney bishop to lead Rockhampton Diocese - CathNews
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has named Bishop Daniel Meagher, auxiliary bishop of Sydney, as the eleventh bishop of the Diocese of Rockhampton. Source: Catholic Weekly.

item.title: Love more powerful than hatred: Bishops' Easter messages - CathNews
item.description: In a world marked by war and violence, cost-of-living pressures and discord, the hope of Easter speaks more powerfully into people’s lives than ever, Australia’s Catholic Bishops have said in their Easter messages.
